items.title: The Extravagance of 1700s Court Dresses | The Spitalfields Mantua Dress
items.description:
In the 18th century, Mantua dresses were the height of court fashion. In this video, our experts discuss a rare and spectacular dress that dates from around 1756. It's 210cm in width, designed to show off how much expensive fabric the wearer could afford. Furthermore, the wider you were, the more likely it would be that you were seen. Few such Mantua dresses have survived from this period, making this a rare treasure within Historic Royal Palaces' collections.

global_silver_linings.title: Chihuahua Won’t Stop Pawing at Her Until Owner Finds the Breast Cancer She Smelled
global_silver_linings.snippet: A dog owner says her pooch saved her life, by repeatedly pawing at her armpit, which eventually alerted her to breast cancer. The 61-year-old says her chihuahua Flag started the odd behavior years ago, constantly hitting the underside of her arm with his paw. She originally dismissed the behavior, until she spotted a small lump […] The post Chihuahua Won’t Stop Pawing at Her Until Owner Finds the Breast Cancer She Smelled appeared first on Good News Network .
global_silver_linings.reason: This little Chihuahua's persistent pawing likely saved her owner's life, a beautiful reminder that the bond between humans and animals can be quietly, profoundly protective. Dogs' extraordinary sense of smell continues to offer real promise in early cancer detection.

global_silver_linings.reason: A teacher's willingness to ask a hard question in public — even at personal cost — shows that everyday people still stand up for accountability in their communities. These quiet acts of civic courage are what keep democracy honest.

global_silver_linings.title: The Great Bubble Barrier: bubble curtains are intercepting 86 percent of river plastic
global_silver_linings.snippet: Rivers are how plastic gets to the ocean. Stop it there, and you stop it for good. The Great Bubble Barrier, a Dutch company, has built a technology to do exactly that.
global_silver_linings.reason: A curtain of rising bubbles guiding river plastic to collection points sounds almost too elegant to be real, yet it's intercepting 86% of waste before it reaches the ocean. Simple, low-disruption solutions like this give genuine reason to believe we can turn the tide on plastic pollution.

featured_read.title: Enchantment and the Courage of Joy: René Magritte on the Antidote to the Banality of Pessimism
featured_read.snippet: "Life is wasted when we make it more terrifying, precisely because it is so easy to do so."
featured_read.blurb: This essay asks why we reach so readily for dread when wonder costs us the same effort — and lets Magritte, of all people, make the case that choosing enchantment is not naïveté but a quiet act of defiance. Clear an unhurried thirty minutes and let it recalibrate what you call realism.

news.title: The Cheap 1-Ingredient Glaze That Completely Transforms Steak
news.snippet: Steak is a staple protein in my repertoire, and I’m always looking for easy ways to dress it up. Simple upgrades, like oyster sauce, can make all the difference when I’m trying to keep things interesting week after week. If you’ve never brushed oyster sauce onto a steak while it sears, then you’re in for a treat.
news.blurb: A single pantry staple turning an everyday steak into something worth talking about — consider our curiosity thoroughly piqued.

news.title: Pollock tacos and hake with saffron aïli and butter beans | Andy Beynon’s summer fish recipes
news.snippet: Perfect for cooking in the heat, these light, fresh dishes that are bursting with flavour will have you falling hook, line and sinker Summer is my favourite time of year to cook fish. There are so many fantastic seasonal species available and, so long as they’re properly fresh and of good quality, they need very little intervention. I often look for lightness, freshness and acidity to bring balance and lift to a summery fish dish, whether that comes from citrus, herbs or a sharp dressing, because those elements enhance the natural flavour of the fish, rather than masking it.
news.blurb: Light, sunshine-friendly fish recipes that make a compelling case for letting the season do most of the heavy lifting in the kitchen.
